root_cause.text: Writing VRR timing registers (TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE) before the corresponding display interface (TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL) is enabled violates the hardware programming sequence required by the BSpec, causing a machine check exception (MCE) hang on ICL platforms.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states, "Apparently ICL may hang with an MCE if we write TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE before enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL." The fix reorders VRR timing configuration from a point before TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL is enabled (hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder) to after it is enabled (intel_vrr_transcoder_enable), and adds a WARN to enforce that TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL is already enabled when programming those registers.

The fix reorders VRR timing configuration from a point before TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL is enabled (hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder) to after it is enabled (intel_vrr_transcoder_enable), and adds a WARN to enforce that TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL is already enabled when programming those registers.

candidates.rationale: This function directly writes the VRR timing registers (TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE) and is called before the display interface (TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL) is enabled, violating the hardware programming sequence required by BSpec and causing MCE hangs on ICL.

This call sets other transcoder timings and appears immediately before the VRR timing write, indicating that the entire timing setup block occurs too early in the sequence, likely before the display interface is enabled.

This conditional controls the subsequent register write (TRANS_MULT) and is part of the same ordering block. If the display interface has not yet been enabled, this write may also be premature, contributing to the sequence violation.

This register write (TRANS_MULT) occurs in the same ordering window as the VRR timing write. Writing any transcoder configuration registers before the display interface is enabled violates the BSpec sequence and can trigger system hangs.

This guard condition sits within a VRR-related function (likely intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings or similar). Although it checks hardware capability, it does not prevent the ordering issue; the actual vulnerable write is allowed to proceed when VRR is present.

This early-return check is in another VRR setup function. While it prevents VRR programming when not possible, it does not enforce the required sequencing relative to the display interface enable, and therefore still permits the vulnerable out-of-order write when VRR is possible.

This conditional controls the subsequent TRANS_MULT register write within the same premature block. Even when true, it allows another transcoder configuration write before the display interface is enabled, further violating the required sequence.

This write to the TRANS_MULT register occurs in the same timing block as the VRR write, before the display interface is enabled. Writing any transcoder configuration register out of order violates the BSpec and can trigger system hangs.

This guard condition controls entry into a VRR-related function that performs the premature VRR register writes. While it checks hardware capability, it does not prevent the ordering issue, and the vulnerable write is executed when VRR is present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings() writes VRR timing registers (e.g., TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE). The vulnerability is that writing these registers before the corresponding display interface (TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL) is enabled causes a machine check exception on ICL.
